title: Partition Operations in CuTe DSL
key_concepts: Partitioning divides tensors among threads, warps, or blocks
Spatial, strided, and hierarchical partitioning types
Partition functions for copy and MMA operations
critical_patterns: Spatial Partitioning: Threads get different spatial regions
Strided Partitioning: Threads get every Nth element
Block-Level Partitioning: Each block processes a tile of the tensor
Thread-Level Partitioning Within Block: Threads further partition data within blocks
2D Partitioning: Partition a 2D tensor among a 2D thread layout
Cyclic Partitioning: Distribute work cyclically for load balancing
code_snippets:
@cute.kernel
def hierarchical_partition(data: cute.Tensor):
    bid = cute.arch.block_idx()[0]
    block_data = data[bid]
    wid = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0] // 32
    warp_data = block_data[wid]
    lane = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0] % 32
    thread_data = warp_data[lane]
    process(thread_data)

@cute.kernel
def partition_source_example(gmem: cute.Tensor, smem: cute.Tensor):
    tiled_copy = cute.make_tiled_copy(...)
    tid = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
    thread_copy = tiled_copy.get_slice(tid)
    thread_src = thread_copy.partition_S(gmem)
    thread_dst = thread_copy.partition_D(smem)
    cute.copy(tiled_copy, thread_src, thread_dst)
constraints: Ensure partitions align with memory boundaries for coalescing
Check bounds to avoid out-of-bounds access
Verify all elements are processed exactly once
compressed_summary: Partitioning in CuTe DSL is crucial for efficient parallel GPU programming, allowing large tensors to be divided among threads, warps, or blocks. The document outlines three main types of partitioning: spatial, strided, and hierarchical. Spatial partitioning assigns different spatial regions to threads, strided partitioning distributes every Nth element, and hierarchical partitioning divides data at multiple levels (block, warp, thread). Key partition functions include partition_S() for source tensors, partition_D() for destination tensors, and partition_A/B/C() for matrices in MMA operations. Practical patterns include block-level partitioning, thread-level partitioning within blocks, 2D partitioning, and cyclic partitioning for load balancing. Code snippets illustrate these patterns, emphasizing the importance of coalesced memory access and balanced workload distribution. Constraints include ensuring memory alignment, bounds checking, and verifying partition coverage to prevent overlaps. Best practices suggest using tiled operations for complex partitioning and avoiding strided access patterns. The document also highlights common mistakes such as incorrect partition sizes and unbalanced partitions, providing guidelines for effective partitioning strategies in GPU kernel development with CuTe DSL.
